claim: A standard atomic force microscope probe tip is thinner than an atom.
claim_boundary: Applies to standard commercial silicon/silicon-nitride AFM probes in normal imaging modes. Does not cover specialized CO-terminated ultrahigh-vacuum non-contact probes, which can approach single-molecule apex sharpness.
finding: Five independent sources report standard AFM tip radius 5-10 nm. Atomic diameter is ~0.1-0.3 nm. The tip is roughly 20-100x wider than an atom: tens of atoms across, not thinner than one.
sources: Springer, Nanomanufacturing and Metrology (2022): standard silicon probes, nominal tip radius 8 nm
NCI Nanotechnology Characterization Laboratory: tip radius of curvature on the order of nanometers
Univ. of Washington Intro SFM lab manual: tip radius ~10 nm
UIUC PHYS 403 AFM lecture (2025): common tip radius of curvature < 10 nm
Rubicon Science AFM overview: tip radius 5-10 nm
